name: Tunnel
description: Named local TCP endpoints that forward to a destination, so consumers point at 127.0.0.1:<port> and never learn what is on the other side. Two destination kinds: a custom IP:port (a plain TCP proxy, working today) and a linked aw-remote-host (needs tcp_* frames on the /link tunnel — not shipped yet, and the UI says so rather than pretending). Each tunnel chooses its own bind address, which is what decides who may use it.

allow_lan_destinations.description: Allow custom-IP tunnels to forward to private/LAN ranges (RFC1918, loopback). Turning this off restricts destinations to public addresses only. A tunnel forwards from inside this workspace, so this is the blast-radius knob: leaving it on is what makes it useful for reaching your own machines, and turning it off is what stops it being a pivot into your private network.

connect_timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for the TCP connection to a tunnel's destination before giving up on one client connection.
